extracted.intended_audience: parents and tutors (especially of the gentry/nobility) seeking practical guidance on educating children
extracted.subtask_description: Advice on selecting tutors and methods for educating children of quality, emphasizing judgment, moral formation, individualized instruction, and practical application over rote learning and mere scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internalize learning (own wisdom)
rubrics_metrics.description: A man can never be wise but by his own wisdom; one may become learned by other men's learning, but never wise except by his own wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor instruction that leads pupils to make knowledge their own rather than merely memorizing others' words. Anti-pattern: pupils who 'take other men's knowledge and opinions upon trust' and remain dependent rather than autonomous thinkers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize knowledge (learning must be applied)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non enim paranda nobis solum, sed fruenda sapientia est — 'For wisdom is not only to be acquired, but to be utilised.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should produce usable conduct and habits; knowledge without practice is of little value. Example: a scholar acquainted with Galen but ignorant of the patient's disease is useless; guidance is to link study with practical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize judgment over mere knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge is not so absolutely necessary as judgment; the last may make shift without the other, but the other never without this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting tutors or assessing pupils, value capacity for judgment and understanding above the volume of facts memorized. Socratic-style discernment and practical reasoning trump rote erudition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer a 'well-made head' to a 'well-filled' one
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Tete bien faite' — seek a pupil with a well-made rather than merely well-filled head; prefer manners and judgment to mere learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For boys of quality, choose tutors and curricula that form composure, sense, and good manners as much as imparting scholastic content. The aim is an accomplished person (e.g., a cavalier), not a walking repository of quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socratic/active method: make the pupil speak first
rubrics_metrics.description: Socrates... made first their scholars speak, and then they spoke to them. Put it to the test, permitting his pupil himself to taste things, and of himself to discern and choose them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use questioning, dialogue, and pupil-led exposition to reveal understanding and cultivate independent thought. Anti-pattern: teacher-centered funneling where the pupil only repeats what was poured in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualize instruction to pupil capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Such as undertake, with one and the same lesson, and the same measure of direction, to instruct several boys of differing and unequal capacities, are infinitely mistaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust pace, content, and expectations to each child's abilities. Example: do not teach a group of unequal learners with identical lessons; this produces very few genuinely educated pupils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess learning by life and practice, not memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Let him judge of the profit he has made, not by the testimony of his memory, but by that of his life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate students by how they apply teachings in behavior and decision-making rather than by their ability to recite grammar or texts. Make moral and practical application the metric of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require transfer and reformulation of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Let him make him put what he has learned into a hundred several forms, and accommodate it to so many several subjects, to see if he yet rightly comprehends it, and has made it his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have pupils restate, adapt, and apply lessons across contexts to test genuine understanding. Anti-pattern: regurgitating the lesson unaltered (crudity and indigestion metaphor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach by works and examples, not only by words
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only by words and precepts, but chiefly by works and examples; to the end it might not be a knowledge in the mind only, but its complexion and habit: not an acquisition, but a natural possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modeling, practice, and lived examples to form habits and character. Institutional examples invoked: Spartan emphasis on acting, Xenophon's Persian regimen, Plato's laws favoring virtue through practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit education to nature and future employments
rubrics_metrics.description: Plato’s principal institution ... to fit his citizens with employments suitable to their nature. 'What they ought to do when they come to be men,' said he.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek to identify natural inclinations and prepare children for roles that suit them (civic, military, administrative), rather than imposing a one-size-fits-all scholarly track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select tutors who emphasize manners and judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The charge of the tutor ... has several duties ... seeking, indeed, both the one and the other, but rather of the two to prefer manners and judgment to mere learning, and that this man should exercise his charge after a new method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appointing a tutor, prioritize a person who cultivates conduct, prudence, and adaptive understanding over someone solely credentialed by book-learning. Example: prefer a tutor who will test and converse rather than only lecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid producing pedants and coxcombs
rubrics_metrics.description: They bring back their soul ... swelled and puffed up with vain and empty shreds and patches of learning ... a greater coxcomb than when he went from home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of educational systems that create superficial scholars who parade quotations but lack judgment or moral sense. Anti-patterns include excessive emphasis on Latin/Greek display, verbose quotations, and formal ornamentation without substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate learning with work; don't tie learning to the soul apart from action
rubrics_metrics.description: We are not to tie learning to the soul, but to work and incorporate them together: not to tincture it only, but to give it a thorough and perfect dye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure intellectual instruction is inseparable from practical exercise and duties so knowledge becomes ingrained habit. A learning divorced from practice may corrupt or be wasted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize moral education (science of goodness) first
rubrics_metrics.description: All other knowledge is hurtful to him who has not the science of goodness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place formation of conscience, justice, temperance, and courage at the center of education. Intellectual attainments without virtue risk being applied poorly or abusively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsider education that worsens the pupil
rubrics_metrics.description: Ut fuerit melius non didicisse — 'So that it were better not to have learned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a course of study does not improve a person's character or capacities, it may be better left undone. Avoid education that makes the pupil 'worse' (more vain, less practical, less virtuous).
